seminar: A Guide to Statistical Network Modeling
scope: Foundations of binary static exponential-family random graph models. Every bundled example is a documented public static network whose support is checked before model fitting.

examples.name: Florentine Families: Business Ties
examples.citation: Padgett, J. F. (1994), as documented in Statnet's ergm florentine data manual.
examples.network_type: Static, undirected, binary, unipartite network of 16 Florentine families.
examples.response_scope: The supplied object is a symmetric binary encoding of business/financial ties. It is not a reconstructed directed flow network.
examples.rationale: A compact historical network for checking support, the edges-only model, and one theory-led actor-covariate extension.
examples.caution: The current packaged flobusiness object has 15 edges; use wealth or priorates cautiously and never use totalties as an exogenous predictor.

examples.name: Sampson Monastery: Liking Nominations, Wave 3
examples.source: Statnet ergm package, samplk3 object; original data by Sampson (1968)
examples.citation: Sampson, S. F. (1968). A novitiate in a period of change. Cornell University doctoral dissertation.
examples.network_type: Static, directed, binary, unipartite network of 18 monk-novitiates.
examples.response_scope: A single binary nomination wave, not the pooled nomination-count object and not a temporal analysis.
examples.rationale: A small directed network for conditional density, reciprocity, and descriptive group-mixing demonstrations.
examples.caution: The fixed-choice nomination design constrains outdegree; group classification is not automatically an exogenous causal covariate.

examples.name: Lazega Law Firm: Advice Network
examples.source: RSiena LazegaLawyers public archive, advice relation
examples.citation: Lazega, E. (2001). The Collegial Phenomenon: The Social Mechanisms of Cooperation Among Peers in a Corporate Law Partnership. Oxford University Press.
examples.network_type: Static, directed, binary, unipartite advice network of 71 lawyers.
examples.response_scope: The advice layer only. In the source coding, i→j means i named j as an adviser; coworker and friendship are separate network outcomes, not default dyadic controls.
examples.rationale: A documented directed professional network with actor attributes for theory-led office, status, seniority, or gender examples.
examples.caution: Treat this as one cross-sectional advice-network snapshot; do not reverse the advice-flow convention or claim causal organization effects.

examples.name: Davis Southern Women: Attendance Affiliation Network
examples.source: Davis, Gardner, and Gardner (1941), public bipartite network as distributed by NetworkX and Statnet
examples.citation: Davis, A., Gardner, B. B., and Gardner, M. R. (1941). Deep South. University of Chicago Press.
examples.network_type: Static, undirected, binary, bipartite woman–event affiliation network with 18 women and 14 events.
examples.response_scope: Edges record attendance, not interpersonal friendship. Only woman–event dyads are admissible in the original network.
examples.rationale: A transparent public two-mode example for defining a bipartite support and fitting bipartite-appropriate baseline terms.
examples.caution: A one-mode projection is a different, usually weighted network; do not fit unipartite triangle terms to the original incidence data.

examples.name: Kapferer Tailor Shop: First-Period Sociational Ties
examples.source: Statnet ergm package, kapferer object; original data by Kapferer (1972)
examples.citation: Kapferer, B. (1972). Strategy and Transaction in an African Factory. Manchester University Press.
examples.network_type: Static, undirected, binary, unipartite network of 39 tailor-shop workers.
examples.response_scope: The packaged kapferer object is the selected 39-worker first-period binary sociational relation, not the instrumental relation or pooled two-wave data.
examples.rationale: A public workplace network for inspecting support, degree structure, and a carefully labelled closure extension.
examples.caution: The edge records relatively frequent sociational interaction; it is neither a valued network nor the full first-period workforce.
